hunks.baseline: Sometimes, life throws you a curveball.
hunks.sol: Sometimes, what you’ve always taken for granted goes wrong.

hunks.baseline: A moment when something you’d always taken for granted—one is followed by two, and two by three—suddenly takes an unexpected turn.
hunks.sol: One comes after two—no, two comes after one, and three after two. Then, without warning, something as certain as that takes a turn you never expected.

hunks.baseline: I froze like a statue and stared blankly at the holographic window floating in the air.
hunks.sol: I froze like a statue and stared at the holographic window floating in the air.

hunks.baseline: Inside its translucent frame, the words on the screen said exactly what I’d just heard.
hunks.sol: Inside its translucent frame were the same words I’d just heard.

hunks.baseline: The two words drilled into my retinas, tearing through the emptiness in my mind and leaving me reeling.
hunks.sol: The words seemed to bore into my eyes, stirring up confusion in my suddenly empty mind.

hunks.baseline: *Why? How could this happen?*
hunks.sol: *Why?*

hunks.baseline: My lips moved on instinct, but no sound came out.
hunks.sol: My lips moved, but no sound came out.

hunks.baseline: With endless questions swirling in my mind, I shook my head. The world spun around me. No matter how I looked at it, I couldn’t make sense of what was happening.
hunks.sol: I shook my head. The world spun. No matter how hard I tried, I couldn’t make sense of what had happened.

hunks.baseline: I wanted that to be the case.
But, unfortunately, the truth was different.
hunks.sol: I wished I were. Unfortunately, this was real.

hunks.baseline: “……Human, snap out of it!”
hunks.sol: “…Human, snap out of it!”

hunks.baseline: A voice reached me through my blurred vision. If the Skeleton King’s hand shaking me was proof that this was all real—
hunks.sol: The Skeleton King’s voice reached me through the haze. His hand shook me, proof that this was reality.

hunks.baseline: The chimes still rang out without stopping. And the darkness, scattering into the air like ash, was proof that one being had been erased.
hunks.sol: The chimes kept ringing, and the darkness scattering into the air like ash was proof that one being had been erased.

hunks.baseline: Another Level Up. And then, recovery.
hunks.sol: Another Level Up. Another recovery.

hunks.baseline: Focus returned to my sight, which had been clouded by thick fog. Energy surged through my revitalized body, stronger than before.
hunks.sol: My foggy vision cleared. Strength surged through my revitalized body, more powerful than before.

hunks.baseline: But none of that mattered to me now.
hunks.sol: None of that mattered.

hunks.baseline: Something else was far more important.
*The Doppelganger was definitely erased. It was.*
hunks.sol: *The Doppelganger was erased. I’m sure of it.*

hunks.baseline: My body was brimming with strength, but my mental reserves had run dry long ago.
hunks.sol: My body was brimming with strength, but my mental reserves had run dry long ago. The shock made me stagger.

hunks.baseline: The shock hit me hard, and I staggered.
Michael Silbert was dead. The Doppelganger was dead. I’d personally eliminated every being that threatened this world.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert was dead. The Doppelganger was dead. With my own hands, I’d eliminated the beings that threatened this world.

hunks.baseline: Even if a new threat came someday, one that would plunge the entire world into a sea of fire, I’d believed we’d at least bought ourselves time for now.
hunks.sol: Even if a new threat came someday and plunged the whole world into fire, I’d believed we could at least buy ourselves some time right now.

hunks.baseline: I couldn’t breathe. A terrible headache stabbed at my brain like an awl, and I remembered the Doppelganger’s final moments. That faint smile I’d thought I’d only imagined.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t breathe. A terrible headache stabbed through my skull like an awl, and I remembered the Doppelganger’s final moments. That faint smile I’d dismissed as a trick of my eyes.

hunks.baseline: *I didn’t see it wrong…*
hunks.sol: *I saw it.*

hunks.baseline: I’d been wrong.
What I’d seen at the end hadn’t been some passing illusion. It was the smile of someone who had finished everything they needed to do.
hunks.sol: I’d been wrong. That smile was real—the smile of someone who had finished what they’d set out to do.

hunks.baseline: Where had things gone wrong? Had I lacked the effort, or the strength?
hunks.sol: Where had things gone wrong? Had I not tried hard enough? Had I not been strong enough?

hunks.baseline: Or had the enormous calamity I’d tried to stop been in preparation for so long that no mere human could have prevented it?
hunks.sol: Or had the calamity I’d tried to stop been in the making for so long that no mere human could have prevented it?

hunks.baseline: I didn’t know. There was nothing I could figure out.
hunks.sol: I didn’t know. I couldn’t tell what had happened.

hunks.baseline: I was only sure of one thing: something that should never have happened had begun.
hunks.sol: I was sure of only one thing: something that should never have happened had begun.

hunks.baseline: A drumbeat suddenly reached my ears.
hunks.sol: A drumbeat reached my ears.

hunks.baseline: It wasn’t a clear chime or a mechanical warning. It was more ominous than anything I’d ever heard—a war drum heralding the dawn of a great war, and a warning from the System.
hunks.sol: Neither a clear chime nor a mechanical warning, it was more ominous than any sound I’d ever heard. A war drum heralding the start of a great war—and a warning from the System.

hunks.baseline: Cursed beings, summoned from another dimension by someone else, had set foot in this world.
hunks.sol: Cursed beings summoned by someone else across a tear between dimensions had set foot in this world.

hunks.baseline: A rift. And magical power surging.
hunks.sol: A rift. Magical power surging.

hunks.baseline: *So this was it. The plan the Doppelganger had been preparing.*
hunks.sol: *So this was the plan the Doppelganger had prepared.*

hunks.baseline: I’d underestimated it far too much.
hunks.sol: I’d underestimated it.

hunks.baseline: It had been clever enough to manipulate the whole world from behind Michael Silbert, to establish itself as a divine being in a vast religion.
hunks.sol: It had manipulated the whole world from behind Michael Silbert and made itself a divine figure in a vast religion. It was that cunning.

hunks.baseline: And I’d thought a creature like that wouldn’t have prepared a failsafe for a plan it had spent over thirty years working on?
hunks.sol: Why had I assumed a creature like that wouldn’t have a failsafe for a plan it had spent more than thirty years preparing?

hunks.baseline: Bombs don’t care who owns them. Whoever holds the switch, the slightest jolt is enough to set one off.
hunks.sol: A bomb doesn’t care who owns it. Whoever holds the switch, the slightest jolt can set it off.

hunks.baseline: My mind went white.
hunks.sol: My mind went blank.

hunks.baseline: The bomb had already gone off, and the rift had begun. This was a calamity that would spread like wildfire, one that couldn’t even be compared to mutation Gates or monster waves.
hunks.sol: The bomb had already gone off. The rift had begun. A calamity beyond anything mutation Gates or monster waves could compare to would spread like wildfire.

hunks.sol: I seized the Skeleton King’s wrist. He’d been watching my inexplicable behavior ever since the Doppelganger died, and now he shouted in confusion.

hunks.baseline: “What are you talking about—”
hunks.sol: “What are you—”

hunks.baseline: “Tell the main force. The World Hunter Federation. Right now.”
hunks.sol: “Tell the main force. Tell the World Hunter Federation. Right now.”

hunks.baseline: My breathing was ragged. The hand gripping the Skeleton King trembled.
hunks.sol: I struggled for breath. My hand trembled around his wrist.

hunks.baseline: “We failed, and the Doppelganger’s plan has come to fruition.”
hunks.sol: “We failed. The Doppelganger’s plan worked.”

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton King tried to haul me up with his powerful hands, but my body went limp against my will.
hunks.sol: The Skeleton King hauled at me with his powerful hands, but my body went limp against my will.

hunks.baseline: After a long fight, as my consciousness sank from exhaustion, I thought of the best thing I could do right now.
hunks.sol: As my consciousness sank after the long fight, I thought of the best thing I could do now.

hunks.baseline: Now I had to return there.
hunks.sol: I had to go back.

hunks.baseline: To the other world that had given me a second life.
To the place where time flowed so slowly that it could delay the flames of calamity.
hunks.sol: To the other world that had given me a second life. To the place where time flowed so slowly that I could delay the flames of calamity.

hunks.baseline: But why was I so sleepy? Why couldn’t I think of anything?
hunks.sol: Why was I so sleepy? Why couldn’t I think?

hunks.baseline: The three syllables I’d always shouted with all my strength scattered into emptiness in my mind.
My thoughts sank beneath the water before I could finish that one short word.
hunks.sol: The three syllables I’d always called out so confidently faded inside my mind. Before I could finish that one short word, my thoughts sank beneath the water.

hunks.baseline: Along with a clear chime, a voice like a hallucination reached my ears.
hunks.sol: A clear chime sounded, followed by a voice that might have been a hallucination.

hunks.baseline: By ordinary standards, his name was long. For a man from the Middle East, it was short. And he was trembling with joy, along with the dozens of companions gathered around him.
hunks.sol: His name was long by ordinary standards and short for a man from the Middle East. He trembled with joy alongside the dozens of companions gathered around him.

hunks.baseline: It had been an unbearably long time. It was true for Ahomed, whose family had followed God’s will for generations, as it was for the others.
hunks.sol: They had endured for so long. Ahomed, whose family had followed God’s will for generations, and all the others.

hunks.baseline: Despite being blessed with a talent for magic that others would have envied, they’d had to live like criminals, hiding from the world. They’d also had to conceal their great plan to change the world’s fate.
hunks.sol: Though they’d been blessed with a talent for magic that anyone would envy, they’d had to hide from the world and live like criminals. They’d had to keep secret their great plan to change the world’s fate.

hunks.baseline: Ahomed felt hot tears running down his face before he even realized it. He had devoted his entire life to following only the Prophet’s words.
hunks.sol: Hot tears ran down Ahomed’s face. He had devoted his entire life to following the Prophet’s words.

hunks.baseline: In the old mage’s eyes lay the relief of someone finally free of all his hardship, the joy of fulfilling God’s mission, and worry and sorrow for someone who wasn’t there.
hunks.sol: In the old mage’s eyes were relief that their hardships were over, joy at fulfilling God’s mission, and worry and sorrow for someone who was not there.

hunks.baseline: He had an inkling of what it meant that the Prophet, who had set out to face the infidels’ army, hadn’t returned.
hunks.sol: He had an inkling of what it meant that the Prophet had not returned from confronting the infidels’ army. But Ahomed kept his feelings to himself.

hunks.baseline: But Ahomed didn’t let those feelings show.
If the Prophet had died, then it was a holy sacrifice to fulfill God’s mission—a martyrdom. He must not grieve.
hunks.sol: If the Prophet had died, it was a holy sacrifice in service of God’s mission. A martyrdom. He must not grieve.

hunks.baseline: No. A great prophet like him would surely have foreseen all of this.
hunks.sol: No. A great prophet like him would surely have foreseen it all.

hunks.baseline: That was why, before he left, he had summoned Ahomed, the one in charge, and urged him to do this.
hunks.sol: That must have been why, before leaving, he had summoned Ahomed, the one in charge, and impressed these instructions upon him.

hunks.sol: Neither the Prophet—no, the Doppelganger—nor Ahomed knew that he would never return. That a single human would erase him forever.

hunks.baseline: They didn’t know that he would never return. That he would be erased forever by the hand of a single human.

But, impossibly, all of it had come to pass. Sensing that something had gone wrong, Ahomed led the mages who had learned from the Prophet alongside him, and they stood before the magic circle they’d been preparing for so long.
hunks.sol: Yet that was exactly what had happened. Sensing that something had gone wrong, Ahomed led the mages who had studied under the Prophet alongside him to the Magic Formation they had spent so long preparing.

hunks.baseline: And now, in this very moment—
They watched the darkness rise, devouring more Magic Gems than they could count.
hunks.sol: And now they watched darkness rise from it, devouring more Magic Gems than they could count.

hunks.sol: “O Messenger of God! O hammer of God, who will set this defiled world right! At last, descend upon us!”

hunks.baseline: In that moment, a cry rang out, filled with a lifetime of resentment and a faith that could only be called fanatical.
hunks.sol: His cry rang out, carrying a lifetime of pent-up anguish and a faith that could only be called fanatical.
